audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for empty tomb, women witnesses, Peter, Emmaus, opened Scriptures, recognized in broken bread, resurrection appearance, opened minds, mission, promise, Bethany blessing/ascension.

verses.restored: On the first day of the week, at deep dawn, they came to the tomb bringing the spices they had prepared.

familiar.text: Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.

modern.text: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.

original.text: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ⸂ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον⸃ φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ⸀ἀρώματα.

verses.restored: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.

familiar.text: And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.

modern.text: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,

original.text: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου,

verses.restored: Entering, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

familiar.text: And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

modern.text: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

original.text: ⸂εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ⸃ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ ⸀σῶμα.

verses.restored: It happened, while they were perplexed about this, look, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments:

modern.text: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ⸀ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ⸂ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ⸃.

verses.restored: As they became afraid and bowed their faces to the earth, they said to them, Why do you seek the living one among the dead?

familiar.text: And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?

modern.text: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?

original.text: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν ⸂τὰ πρόσωπα⸃ εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς· Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;

verses.restored: He is not here, but was raised. Remember how he spoke to you while still in Galilee,

familiar.text: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,

modern.text: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:

original.text: ⸂οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη.⸃ μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ,

verses.restored: saying that the Son of Humanity must be handed over into hands of sinful/misaligned humans, be crucified, and on the third day rise.

familiar.text: Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

modern.text: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”

original.text: λέγων ⸂τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ⸃ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.

verses.restored: They remembered his words.

familiar.text: And they remembered his words,

modern.text: Then they remembered His words.

original.text: καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: Returning from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.

familiar.text: And returned from the sepulchre, and told all these things unto the eleven, and to all the rest.

modern.text: And when they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.

original.text: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.

verses.restored: Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them; they were saying these things to the apostles.

familiar.text: It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, which told these things unto the apostles.

modern.text: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.

original.text: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ⸀ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς· ⸀ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.

verses.restored: These words appeared before them like nonsense, and they were not trusting them.

familiar.text: And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not.

modern.text: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.

original.text: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ⸀ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.

verses.restored: But Peter, rising, ran to the tomb; stooping, he sees the linen cloths alone, and he went away to himself, marveling at what had happened.

familiar.text: Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.

modern.text: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened. The Road to Emmaus (Mark 16:12–13)

original.text: ⸂Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ⸀ὀθόνια μόνα· καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς ⸀αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός.⸃

verses.restored: Look, two of them were traveling that same day to a village named Emmaus, about sixty stadia from Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs.

modern.text: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.

original.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ⸂ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι⸃ εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς,

verses.restored: They were speaking with one another about all these things that had happened.

familiar.text: And they talked together of all these things which had happened.

modern.text: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.

original.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.

verses.restored: It happened, while they were speaking and discussing, Jesus himself drew near and traveled with them.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.

modern.text: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ ⸀αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς,

verses.restored: But their eyes were held back so that they did not recognize him.

familiar.text: But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.

modern.text: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He said to them, What are these words you are exchanging with one another as you walk? They stood still, looking sad.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?

modern.text: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stood still, with sadness on their faces.

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες; καὶ ⸀ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.

verses.restored: One named Cleopas answered him, Are you the only one dwelling near Jerusalem who does not know the things that happened in it in these days?

familiar.text: And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days?

modern.text: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ⸂εἷς ὀνόματι⸃ Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;

verses.restored: He said to them, What things? They said to him, The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who became a man prophet powerful in work and word before the Divine and all the people,

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people:

modern.text: “What things?” He asked. “The events involving Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. “This man was a prophet, powerful in speech and action before God and all the people.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ποῖα; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ ⸀Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ,

verses.restored: and how our chief priests and rulers handed him over to a judgment of death and crucified him.

familiar.text: And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him.

modern.text: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.

original.text: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: But we had hoped that he was the one about to redeem Israel. Yet with all these things, this is the third day since these things happened.

familiar.text: But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel: and beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done.

modern.text: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.

original.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε ⸀καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ⸀ἄγει ἀφʼ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.

verses.restored: But also certain women from among us astonished us, having come early to the tomb.

familiar.text: Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre;

modern.text: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,

original.text: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ⸀ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον

verses.restored: Not finding his body, they came saying they had also seen a vision of messengers who say he lives.

familiar.text: And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive.

modern.text: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.

original.text: καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.

verses.restored: Some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women said, but him they did not see.

familiar.text: And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not.

modern.text: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”

original.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθόν τινες τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εὗρον οὕτως καθὼς ⸀καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες εἶπον, αὐτὸν δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.

verses.restored: He said to them, O uncomprehending ones, and slow of heart to trust upon all that the prophets spoke.

familiar.text: Then he said unto them, O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken:

modern.text: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, how slow are your hearts to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

original.text: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησαν οἱ προφῆται·

verses.restored: Was it not necessary for the Messiah to suffer these things and enter into his glory?

familiar.text: Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?

modern.text: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”

original.text: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

familiar.text: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

modern.text: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.

original.text: καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν προφητῶν ⸀διερμήνευσεν αὐτοῖς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γραφαῖς τὰ περὶ ⸀ἑαυτοῦ.

verses.restored: They drew near to the village where they were going, and he acted as though he were going farther.

familiar.text: And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and he made as though he would have gone further.

modern.text: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.

original.text: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς ⸀προσεποιήσατο ⸀πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.

verses.restored: They urged him strongly, saying, Remain with us, because it is toward evening and the day has already declined. He went in to remain with them.

familiar.text: But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them.

modern.text: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.” So He went in to stay with them.

original.text: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Μεῖνον μεθʼ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ⸀ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα. καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: It happened, when he reclined with them, taking the bread, he blessed, broke, and gave it to them.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them.

modern.text: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετʼ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·

verses.restored: Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him; and he became invisible from them.

familiar.text: And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.

modern.text: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus—and He disappeared from their sight.

original.text: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: They said to one another, Was not our heart burning within us as he was speaking to us on the way, as he was opening the Scriptures to us?

familiar.text: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

modern.text: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

original.text: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Οὐχὶ ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν καιομένη ἦν ⸂ἐν ἡμῖν⸃ ὡς ἐλάλει ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ⸀ὡς διήνοιγεν ἡμῖν τὰς γραφάς;

verses.restored: Rising that same hour, they returned to Jerusalem and found the eleven gathered together and those with them,

familiar.text: And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them,

modern.text: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and those with them, gathered together

original.text: καὶ ἀναστάντες αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ εὗρον ⸀ἠθροισμένους τοὺς ἕνδεκα καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς,

verses.restored: saying, The Lord was truly raised and appeared to Simon.

familiar.text: Saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.

modern.text: and saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”

original.text: λέγοντας ὅτι ⸂ὄντως ἠγέρθη ὁ κύριος⸃ καὶ ὤφθη Σίμωνι.

verses.restored: They described the things on the way and how he was known to them in the breaking of the bread.

familiar.text: And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.

modern.text: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread. Jesus Appears to the Disciples (John 20:19–23; 1 John 1:1–4)

original.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐξηγοῦντο τὰ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καὶ ὡς ἐγνώσθη αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου.

verses.restored: As they were speaking these things, he himself stood in their midst and said to them, Peace to you.

familiar.text: And as they thus spake, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

modern.text: While they were describing these events, Jesus Himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”

original.text: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων ⸀αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ ⸀αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: Startled and becoming afraid, they thought they were beholding a spirit.

familiar.text: But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

modern.text: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.

original.text: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν.

verses.restored: He said to them, Why are you troubled, and why do reasonings rise in your heart?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?

modern.text: “Why are you troubled,” Jesus asked, “and why do doubts arise in your hearts?

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν ⸂τῇ καρδίᾳ⸃ ὑμῶν;

verses.restored: See my hands and my feet, that I myself am; touch me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you behold me having.

familiar.text: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.

modern.text: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see—for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”

original.text: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου ὅτι ⸂ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός⸃· ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι πνεῦμα σάρκα καὶ ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα.

verses.restored: [Saying this, he showed them the hands and the feet.]

familiar.text: And when he had thus spoken, he shewed them his hands and his feet.

modern.text: And when He had said this, He showed them His hands and feet.

original.text: ⸂[καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ⸀ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.]⸃

verses.restored: While they were still not trusting from joy and were marveling, he said to them, Do you have anything edible here?

familiar.text: And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, he said unto them, Have ye here any meat?

modern.text: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement, He asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”

original.text: ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε;

verses.restored: They gave him a piece of broiled fish.

familiar.text: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.

modern.text: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ ⸀μέρος·

verses.restored: Taking it, he ate before them.

familiar.text: And he took it, and did eat before them.

modern.text: and He took it and ate it in front of them.

original.text: καὶ λαβὼν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἔφαγεν.

verses.restored: He said to them, These are my words that I spoke to you while still with you: that it is necessary for all things written in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and Psalms concerning me to be fulfilled.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.

modern.text: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”

original.text: Εἶπεν δὲ ⸂πρὸς αὐτούς⸃· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ⸀μου οὓς ἐλάλησα πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔτι ὢν σὺν ὑμῖν, ὅτι δεῖ πληρωθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσέως ⸀καὶ προφήταις καὶ ψαλμοῖς περὶ ἐμοῦ.

verses.restored: Then he opened their mind to understand the Scriptures.

familiar.text: Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures,

modern.text: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.

original.text: τότε διήνοιξεν αὐτῶν τὸν νοῦν τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς γραφάς,

verses.restored: He said to them, Thus it has been written: the Messiah suffers and rises from the dead on the third day,

familiar.text: And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day:

modern.text: And He told them, “This is what is written: The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι οὕτως ⸀γέγραπται παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ,

verses.restored: and turning/realignment for release of sins/misalignments is proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

modern.text: and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.

original.text: καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν ⸀καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη— ⸀ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ·

verses.restored: You are witnesses of these things.

familiar.text: And ye are witnesses of these things.

modern.text: You are witnesses of these things.

original.text: ὑμεῖς ⸀ἐστε μάρτυρες τούτων.

verses.restored: Look, I am sending the promise of my Father upon you; but you remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.

familiar.text: And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.

modern.text: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you. But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.” The Ascension (Mark 16:19–20; Acts 1:6–11)

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ⸀ἐξαποστέλλω τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρός μου ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς· ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ ⸀πόλει ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε ⸂ἐξ ὕψους δύναμιν⸃.

verses.restored: He led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.

familiar.text: And he led them out as far as to Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.

modern.text: When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany, He lifted up His hands and blessed them.

original.text: Ἐξήγαγεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ⸀ἕως ⸀πρὸς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ἐπάρας τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: It happened, as he blessed them, he parted from them and was carried up into heaven.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.

modern.text: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν αὐτοὺς διέστη ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ⸂[καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν]⸃.

verses.restored: They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.

familiar.text: And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy:

modern.text: And they worshiped Him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,

original.text: καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸂[προσκυνήσαντες αὐτὸν]⸃ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ μετὰ χαρᾶς μεγάλης,

verses.restored: They were continually in the temple, blessing the Divine.

familiar.text: And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

modern.text: praising God continually in the temple.

original.text: καὶ ἦσαν διὰ παντὸς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ⸀εὐλογοῦντες τὸν ⸀θεόν.
